source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Insulin pens being considered to carry fairly little risk of cross-contamination when they happen to be shared between different clients","B":"Insulin pens being specifically designed and manufactured for safe, repeated use across multiple different clients on a busy unit","C":"This particular practice being considered a fairly standard and widely accepted part of everyday insulin administration on most units","D":"Even with a new needle each time, the pen cartridge itself can become contaminated with blood, posing a bloodborne pathogen transmission risk between clients"}}
source_row.rationale: Insulin pens are intended for single-client use only; even with a new needle for each injection, the pen cartridge itself can become contaminated with blood, posing a serious bloodborne pathogen transmission risk if shared between clients.
source_row.source_detail: Single-Client Use Requirement for Insulin Pens
source_row.source_name: CDC — Insulin Pen Safety and Injection Safety Guidance
